song.title: Full Of The Joys!
song.author: Mark, Helen and Naomi Johnson
song.summary: This ‘happy-go-lucky’ song is a perfect fit for the season, but one that is also well-suited to any upbeat or celebratory kind of day. The chorus comprises a variety of expressions that capture the feeling of being joyful. It is great for language work, and very hard to sing without smiling!
song.teachingTips:
• This song is guaranteed to bring a smile and a sense of joy to both singers and audience! It needs to be sung with loads of energy and bounce.
  • Point out the variation to the melody on ‘free as a bird’ in the chorus, and enjoy how this is different to the melody of ‘we’re tickety-boo’.
  • Notice that on the penultimate chorus, the last line ‘We’re full of the joys of spring!’ is only sung once.

assembly.title: Light and Colour
assembly.description: This assembly encourages us to open our eyes to the colours of springtime, talking about our favourite colours, noticing the extra daylight and appreciating nature's use of colour and light.

assembly.title: Extra Energy
assembly.description: What wakes you up in the morning? From birdsong to sprouting leaves and Easter eggs, this assembly helps us to celebrate all the energy of springtime.

assembly.title: Feeling Hopeful
assembly.description: This assembly explores the meaning of hope and what it will take to realize our ambitions for the future.

assembly.title: Feeling Awake
assembly.description: This assembly uses The Parable of the Sower to reflect on what is needed to be ‘awake and ready for action’ in school.

assembly.title: Feeling Good
assembly.description: This assembly explores the uniqueness of human beings and how we can help others to feel more valuable.

resources.title: Acrostic Spring Poem
resources.content:
[{"key":"482384050edd82de","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Compose an Acrostic Spring Poem. As a class, brainstorm and collect ideas for each of the letters of SPRING. Then, ask the children to write some SPRING poems developing their favourite ideas/words into a line for each letter. 

  • Sunshine peeping through the grey,
  • Petals sprouting, on their way.
  • Rainbows arching overhead, 
  • Insects waking from their beds,
  • New life blooming everywhere,
  • Growing wild, without a care!
","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}}]

Xylophones, glockenspiels or keyboards

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"75c6f8055ebefacf","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Look at the notation for the chorus as you play the vocal track:

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"c1fd734dca96bab1","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicActivities/musicalvariations-1672750356l5pWV.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"8281fb2ae28a7062","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Show the children how the ‘free as a bird’ melody has been altered or ‘varied’ from its first appearance on ‘we're tickety-boo’. This comes as a bit of a surprise and so makes your ears prick up!

Now give out xylophones, glockenspiels or keyboards. Can they play the ‘coz life is a wonderful thing’ line? (Transposed into F major for ease.)

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"3dfd58854d0eeb84","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicActivities/musicalvariations2-1672750357nRXz6.png","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"e341228a0c8b8a57","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Now see if the children can create their own variation by changing one or more of the notes of the melody. Ask for volunteers to demonstrate their version to the class.

","title":"","noMargin":false}},{"key":"bff78be280266c98","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Explain that composers often write a theme and variations, where the main melody, harmony or instrumentation is altered to create interest. Listen to some extracts from famous classical themes and variations, e.g.

  • The Young Person’s Guide To The Orchestra – Benjamin Britten
  • 12 Variations on ‘Ah, vous dirai-je, Maman’ (also known as ‘Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star’) – W.A.Mozart

resources.summary: Notice the melodic variation in the chorus and listen to examples of other themes and variations. Create your own variation by changing one or more of the notes of the melody, using tuned percussion instruments or keyboards.
